notes: Only original n_o, es_value_o, pval_value_o are assigned. Replication and reported_success are unassigned placeholders. No candidate is selected by numeric matching or input order. Candidate results on printed p. 404: fully-mediated model chi-square 781.65 [280], p < .001; nested comparison delta chi-square 7.76 [4], ns. Direct paths to trust: contingent reward beta .57, p < .01; contingent punishment beta −.03, not significant; non-contingent reward beta .14, p < .05; non-contingent punishment beta −.29, p < 01 (canonical text omits decimal in this span; rendered PDF also prints <01). Trust to OCB beta .48, p < .01. Indirect effects on OCB through trust: contingent reward beta .27, p < .01; contingent punishment beta −.01, ns; non-contingent reward beta .07, p < .05; non-contingent punishment beta −.14, p < .05. Hypotheses 1 and 2 compare path confidence intervals rather than print a separate contrast p: contingent reward .49 to .65 versus non-contingent reward .08 to .20; contingent punishment −.01 to .07 versus non-contingent punishment −.34 to −.24 (retain printed values). Footnote 2 gives another model chi-square 1782.32 [607], p < .001 and paths from trust to Altruism .36, Courtesy .54, Civic Virtue .28, Sportsmanship .47, all p < .01. Beta is retained as printed; no conversion is performed. Rendered PDF p. 6 Fig. 1 describes its parameters as a completely standardized solution, but that figure text is absent from the canonical text; no synthesized quotation is supplied. Table 1 on printed p. 405 explicitly reports N = 475 and multiple correlations, adding further potential targets if p. 5 refers to a printed page suffix rather than PDF page. This N is candidate evidence only for parent field-scope review; no critical target-specific analytic N is asserted. Method reports 475 employees and 44 supervisor raters, with no sum; neither df nor generic recruitment totals are used to derive analytic N. Rendered PDF pages 5 and 6 inspected for layout and printed p bounds.
